name: Barkos
overview: Barkos is a male descendant of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role highlights his involvement in the religious duties associated with the temple, as noted in Ezra 2:53. There are no additional notes about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Barkos means "son of Kos," indicating a patronymic origin rather than a name given directly by God. This name is recorded in Ezra 2:53 and does not carry a special theological meaning beyond its literal sense.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Barkos as a descendant of the tribe of Levi, linking him to the Levitical priestly lineage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Barkos's significance lies in his service as a temple servant within the Levitical community. His mention in Ezra 2:53 places him among those who returned from exile to reestablish temple worship, underscoring the continuity of priestly duties and the restoration of proper worship in Israel. Though briefly noted, his role reflects the faithfulness of the Levites in maintaining God's ordinances.
